title: Agent map
description: After a Claude Code mod shared on r/ClaudeAI (reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1xst2qe) that draws a live map of what the agent is doing. What a coding agent is working on, as a map: the agent in the middle with how full its context is, the things it reaches for (you, the model, memory, files, the shell, the network, other agents) evenly round it, and every call going out along a line. A node lights up in ink as it is used: its count, a turning ring while a call to it runs (the agent tree's working mark), a dot travelling out along its line (on the motion tokens, so it follows the book's slow motion; under reduced motion there is no dot and the ring holds still), and its failed calls as an inverted number on its corner. A call from another node (a subagent reading files) draws a curve between the two. Selecting a node puts its line in copper and narrows the log to its calls. A call is running, done or failed; blocked counts as failed. Parts: AgentMap (nodes, calls, context, bind:selected), AgentMapGraph (the map; an icon snippet per node), AgentMapHub (the agent; its name is yours), AgentMapStatus (one line: what runs now, read out as it changes) and AgentMapLog (every call, newest first; empty and no-results said apart). The app feeds it calls; the item draws them and keeps nothing.
